record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.original_question: For DTCS(n), the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree, study the combinatorics of fringe clades by determining the distribution of the number K_n of distinct clade shapes that appear at least once, the size of the largest clade shape that appears more than once, and the size of the smallest clade shape that does not appear at all.

evidence.quote: Regarding the number Nn(χ) of copies of a clade χ in DTCS(n), one could study distributions of the following:

Open Problem 7 . • The number Kn := Pχ 1(Nn(χ)≥1) of different-shape clades within (a realization of ) DTCS(n). • The largest clade that appears more than once within DTCS(n). • The smallest clade that does not appear within DTCS(n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the discrete-time critical beta-splitting random tree DTCS(n) on n ≥ 2 leaves, defined recursively as follows. Start with a root clade of size n. A clade of size m ≥ 2 is split into two child clades of sizes i and m − i (1 ≤ i ≤ m − 1) with probability
  q(m, i) = (1 / h_{m−1}) · 1/(i (m − i)),
where h_{m−1} = Σ_{j=1}^{m−1} 1/(j(m−j)) is the normalizing constant. Each child clade is recursively split by the same rule, and clades of size 1 are leaves. The resulting rooted binary tree has n leaves.

A "clade shape" χ is the unlabeled rooted binary tree shape of a subtree rooted at some internal node (a fringe subtree). For a realization of DTCS(n) and a clade shape χ, let N_n(χ) denote the number of internal nodes of DTCS(n) whose fringe subtree has shape χ. Define:

(a) K_n = Σ_χ 1{N_n(χ) ≥ 1}, the number of distinct clade shapes that appear at least once in DTCS(n).

(b) L_n = max{|χ| : N_n(χ) ≥ 2}, the size (number of leaves) of the largest clade shape that appears more than once in DTCS(n).

(c) S_n = min{|χ| : N_n(χ) = 0}, the size of the smallest clade shape that does not appear at all in DTCS(n).

Determine the distributions (and/or asymptotic behavior as n → ∞) of the random variables K_n, L_n, and S_n.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem about the combinatorics of fringe clades in the critical beta-splitting model. Subsequent work on this model (e.g., a third installment on the exchangeable partition representation and the fringe tree, and a contraction-based approach to critical beta-splitting) develops fringe-tree limit theory but does not appear to resolve the specific distributional questions about K_n (number of distinct clade shapes), the largest repeated clade shape, or the smallest missing clade shape. No published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Overview and open problems on the critical beta-splitting random tree, including questions on counts of clade shapes.
status_evidence.claim: The questions on K_n, the largest repeated clade shape, and the smallest missing clade shape are listed as open problems.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree III: The exchangeable partition representation and the fringe tree
status_evidence.snippet: Develops the exchangeable partition representation and limit fringe tree but does not resolve the specific counting questions on distinct/repeated/missing clade shapes.
status_evidence.claim: Further developments on fringe trees do not appear to settle these specific combinatorial distributional problems.

status_evidence.title: Critical beta-splitting, via contraction
status_evidence.snippet: Alternative contraction-based analysis of the critical beta-splitting tree.
status_evidence.claim: Provides analytic tools but does not resolve the clade-shape counting open problem.
